summary: R2 closures for NEW-MIN-001 and NEW-MIN-002 are real. NEW-MAJ-001's stated fix — the cascade-status carve-out — is substantively present in the plan-doc but is incomplete: the conflict-close CI check verifies only TF-reference presence, with no check that the branch-protection log was NOT modified (i.e., no invocation-footprint absence check). This means a cascade slice can declare cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict, invoke enable-required-check.sh, commit the resulting log entry in the same PR, file the TF reference, and pass the CI check — the API mutation goes undetected and unlogged under the audit trail that the carve-out is supposed to preserve. The R3 surface scan finds one new MAJ on this exact path. Three additional questions from the package (TF-024X-renovate filing-vs-closing, TF-024X-conflict filing-vs-closing before sub-slice, duplicate cascade-status onboarded declarations) are resolved at MIN or lower. R3 fixpoint criterion: 0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ — not met.

findings.title: NEW-MAJ-001 closure verification: cascade-status carve-out for blocked-on-adopter-conflict — PARTIALLY CLOSED; residual invocation-footprint bypass (see R3-NEW-MAJ-001)
findings.evidence: Invariant 2 now reads: 'cascade-slice PRs that declare cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict in DISPATCH-NOTE skip the log-entry assertion (no enable-required-check.sh was invoked because the conflict was discovered before invocation), but MUST instead reference the filed TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF in the DISPATCH-NOTE — the CI script verifies the TF reference exists and matches the standardised prefix.' §5.2 item (2) now requires the cascade-status: field in the DISPATCH-NOTE header taking one of two values. §6 024B acceptance row enumerates both close-states and the operator-bump fallback path. R-024-06 mitigation was rewritten (see R3-VERIFY-NEW-MIN-001 below). The structural incompatibility identified by R2 NEW-MAJ-001 — that a conflict-close PR has no log entry to commit and would be rejected by the old invariant 2 CI clause — is resolved: the conflict-close path is now explicitly scoped out of the log-entry assertion. However, the replacement CI check for conflict-close PRs (TF-reference presence only) does NOT verify that the branch-protection log was not modified in that PR. The plan-doc does not require the CI script to assert log-file unmodified for conflict-close slices. This residual gap is the subject of R3-NEW-MAJ-001.
findings.outcome: PARTIAL — the incompatibility is resolved but the bypass surface introduced by the carve-out is unaddressed; see R3-NEW-MAJ-001

findings.title: NEW-MIN-001 closure verification: R-024-06 CLOSES language — CLOSED
findings.evidence: R-024-06 mitigation in the plan-doc §7 now reads: 'T-024-10 mitigation: cascade slice CLOSES with status blocked-on-adopter-conflict per invariant 10 (forward TF TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> owned by the slice author; new sub-slice opens on conflict resolution). The CI invocation-log check (invariant 2 carve-out) skips log-entry assertion for these close-state slices but verifies the TF reference is present.' The word 'defers' is gone. The language is consistent with invariant 10 and T-024-10. FIX-ROUND-2.md claim matches.

findings.title: NEW-MIN-002 closure verification: TF-024X-renovate STATUS.md row standard + CI verification — CLOSED
findings.evidence: R-024-07 mitigation now reads: 'the cascade slice MUST file a forward TF (TF-024X-renovate-<adopter>) as a STATUS.md Tracked-forward items row using exactly the standardised prefix TF-024X-renovate- followed by the adopter's <owner>-<repo> slug (the check-invocation-log-entry.sh CI script — extended at 024B per the invariant 2 enforcement clause — verifies STATUS.md contains the matching TF row when DISPATCH-NOTE declares the operator-bump fallback).' §5.2 item (2) names the row as a deliverable. §6 024B acceptance row enumerates the operator-bump fallback path as a third check enforced by the CI script. The TF tracking location (STATUS.md Tracked-forward items) is now specified. The CI verification mechanism (check-invocation-log-entry.sh checking STATUS.md for the matching row) is now specified. FIX-ROUND-2.md claim matches.

findings.title: conflict-close CI carve-out verifies only TF-reference presence — no invocation-footprint absence check; a cascade slice can invoke enable-required-check.sh, commit the log entry, declare blocked-on-adopter-conflict, and pass the CI gate
findings.evidence: Invariant 2's conflict-close CI check is specified as: 'the CI script verifies the TF reference exists and matches the standardised prefix.' No additional check is specified. The plan-doc's rationale for the carve-out is: 'no enable-required-check.sh was invoked because the conflict was discovered before invocation' — this is a narrative assertion, not a machine-verified property. The CI script (check-invocation-log-entry.sh, landing at 024B) is spec'd to parse cascade-status: and apply the appropriate check; for blocked-on-adopter-conflict the 'appropriate check' is TF-reference presence only. The spec does not require the script to also assert: (a) docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified in this PR diff, or (b) no new entry matching the PR's target adopter appears in the log file. Consequence: a cascade-slice PR can include both a new log entry (from enable-required-check.sh invocation) AND a TF reference (to satisfy the conflict-close check), declare cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict, and merge without the log-entry CI check ever firing. The API mutation is invisible to the audit trail: the log entry is committed under the conflict-close exemption path, and the onboarded CI path (which would verify the log entry's target matches the DISPATCH-NOTE target) is bypassed by the cascade-status declaration. This is the specific bypass surface the R3 package asked about: 'does the cascade-status field create a path for a malicious slice to declare blocked-on-adopter-conflict to skip the log-entry check while actually invoking enable-required-check.sh?' The answer from the current plan-doc spec is: yes, because the conflict-close CI check has no invocation-footprint absence check.
findings.recommendation: Amend the invariant 2 conflict-close CI spec to require that check-invocation-log-entry.sh ALSO asserts, for cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict PRs: docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified in this PR diff (i.e., git diff shows zero additions to that file). If the log file WAS modified in a conflict-close PR, the CI script must FAIL with an error message indicating that log-file modification is incompatible with blocked-on-adopter-conflict status. Amend §6 024B acceptance row to require: 'check-invocation-log-entry.sh rejects conflict-close PRs where branch-protection-log.md was modified (log-file-presence-in-diff is incompatible with blocked-on-adopter-conflict status)' as a fourth enumerated check. This closes the invocation-footprint bypass path. The fix does not require checking API call traces — git PR diff is sufficient because enable-required-check.sh emits its log block for the operator to paste in; if the operator invoked the script, the log entry appears in the PR diff.

findings.title: Package question: TF-024X-renovate filing vs closing — Threshold A requires CLOSED TF + real Renovate cycle; filing is not sufficient; mechanism is reviewer-dependent at 024G
findings.evidence: R-024-07: 'The adopter is not credited toward Threshold A until that TF closes + a real Renovate cycle has merged + observed clean.' §8 Threshold A row 3: 'Adopters who satisfied the per-slice bake via an operator-driven bump (R-024-07 fallback) do NOT count toward Threshold A until a real Renovate cycle has also merged + observed clean.' Filing a STATUS.md row is NOT sufficient for Threshold A credit — the TF must close AND a real Renovate cycle must have merged. The real Renovate cycle is independently verifiable (a merged Renovate PR with the updated SHA pin, observable in the adopter's PR history). The 024G orchestrator slice has 3-lens R1+R2, and the completeness/correctness lenses must verify per-adopter Threshold A criteria. However, the plan-doc does not define what machine-verifiable state constitutes a STATUS.md TF row being 'closed' — TF closure is a manual row annotation ('Status: closed' or equivalent), which can be authored without actually fixing Renovate. The safeguard is that the 024G reviewer must also verify the real Renovate PR exists on the adopter repo. This is reviewer-dependent rather than CI-enforced. Assessed as MIN — the real Renovate cycle requirement is independently verifiable, and the 024G R1+R2 adversarial review is the structured backstop.
findings.outcome: MIN — not escalating to MAJ; the Threshold A real-Renovate-cycle requirement is independently verifiable by the 024G reviewer; no plan-doc change strictly required but the ambiguity in what constitutes TF closure for STATUS.md rows is a weak link; addressed adequately at 024G review tier

findings.title: Package question: TF-024X-conflict filing vs closing before follow-up sub-slice — plan-doc does not explicitly require TF closure before sub-slice opens; the sub-slice review is the backstop
findings.evidence: Invariant 10: 'when the conflict is resolved, a NEW cascade sub-slice opens for that adopter.' This sentence implies the conflict must be resolved before the sub-slice opens, but 'resolved' is not defined as TF-024X-conflict CLOSED in the STATUS.md. A sub-slice could technically open while the TF is still filed-but-open, with the adopter conflict still unresolved. The sub-slice would have its own 3-lens R1+R2 review, and the safety/correctness lenses would catch an unresolved conflict (if the adopter still has the conflicting workflow). However, the plan-doc does not explicitly state: 'the sub-slice MUST NOT open until TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> is closed.' Assessed as MIN — the R1+R2 adversarial review on the sub-slice is the structural backstop; a sub-slice opening against an adopter with an unresolved conflict would fail the adopter wrapper PR (the conflicting workflow still exists) and the cascade slice could not declare onboarded. The failure mode self-corrects through the process; the gap is the absence of an explicit textual gate.
findings.outcome: MIN — not escalating to MAJ; the sub-slice cannot reach onboarded close-state against a genuinely unresolved conflict; no plan-doc change strictly required at this tier

findings.title: Package question: duplicate cascade-status: onboarded declarations for the same adopter — plan-doc does not prevent two slices from both declaring onboarded for the same adopter
findings.evidence: The plan-doc assigns one named cascade slice per adopter (024C=PIM, 024D=CT, 024E=mapp-doc-agent+recommender, 024F=shopify-app). A conflict-close path produces a sub-slice; the original slice closes with blocked-on-adopter-conflict and the sub-slice closes with onboarded. Two onboarded closures for the same adopter would require two distinct PR sequences, each with a distinct log entry in branch-protection-log.md. check-invocation-log-entry.sh verifies that the PR modifies the log file with a matching entry — it does not check for pre-existing entries for the same adopter. Two log entries for the same adopter + branch would be visible to the 024G reviewer. The enable-required-check.sh script is idempotent (re-running against an already-protected repo applies the same settings; no destructive mutation). Duplicate onboarded declarations are an audit-integrity concern (two entries, one PR referencing each) but not a security bypass — the branch protection state is idempotent, the log file accumulates both entries, and the 024G reviewer counts adopters by log-entry presence. An attacker who files a duplicate onboarded slice gains nothing: the branch protection is already enabled, and both log entries are visible. Assessed as NIT.
findings.outcome: NIT — no new surface beyond audit verbosity; not escalating

r3_verdict_rationale: R3 found 1 new MAJ (R3-NEW-MAJ-001: conflict-close CI carve-out has no invocation-footprint absence check, enabling a bypass where a malicious cascade slice invokes enable-required-check.sh and escapes the audit trail by declaring blocked-on-adopter-conflict). This directly answers the package's primary safety question affirmatively: the cascade-status field DOES create a path for a malicious slice to invoke the script while skipping the log-entry check, because the conflict-close CI check verifies only TF-reference presence, not log-file unmodified. The R3 fixpoint criterion (0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ) is not met. Fix required: amend the invariant 2 conflict-close CI spec to require check-invocation-log-entry.sh to assert that branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified in a blocked-on-adopter-conflict PR diff. Once that fix lands, R3 must run a verification cycle.
r2_closures_verified: 3/3 (NEW-MAJ-001 partial — underlying incompatibility resolved but bypass surface introduced by the carve-out is unaddressed; NEW-MIN-001 closed; NEW-MIN-002 closed)
